title: Main-sequence dust dimmers have wide stellar companions as often as matched Gaia DR3 field stars: 91 dimmers against 15,162 controls reject companion-driven models for most dimmers
abstract: Question: Deep aperiodic dust dimming of mature main-sequence stars is rare, and its cause is not known. Models with an occulting disc around a companion or with a late, tide-driven wide-binary instability predict that dimmers have stellar companions more often than normal stars. We tested this prediction. Approach: We used 91 dimmers: the 81 ZTF main-sequence dipper candidates of Tzanidakis et al. (2025) and 10 dust-like field-dwarf dimmers from prior campaign studies, including Gaia20cdd. For each dimmer we selected matched Gaia DR3 controls in the same field (same G, BP-RP and parallax; 15,162 controls in total). We searched co-moving companions from 1 arcsec to 20,000 au, measured chance alignments at shifted positions, and compared RUWE, image parameters, non-single-star flags and tangential velocities. Results: 13 dimmers have a resolved companion, and the controls predict 10.9 (odds ratio 1.25, 95 percent interval 0.65-2.24). A strict search finds 1 against 2.3 expected. Most dimmer companions are faint chance alignments at 12,000-20,000 au. Search limits of 5,000 and 50,000 au give the same result. With a completeness model, the companion fraction at 100-20,000 au (mass ratio 0.1-1) is 0.063 (0.004-0.27) for dimmers and 0.113 (0.099-0.128) for controls. If every dimmer had such a companion, the strict search would find 15.7, or 7.9 at half completeness (P(<=1) = 0.002). RUWE > 1.4 occurs in 5 dimmers against 3.6 expected; no dimmer has a non-single-star solution. Tangential-velocity ranks are uniform (KS p = 0.81), so the dimmers are not kinematically young. One lead: the M0 dwarf Gaia DR3 2698173741829957888 has an image harmonic amplitude (0.987) above all controls, which can show a close neighbour, but its strong variability may also cause it. Conclusion: In the tested range, dimmers have wide stellar companions as often as matched field stars; models in which most dimmers need a wide stellar companion are rejected. Limitations: companions below about 100 au, brown dwarfs and planets are not tested; the completeness model is approximate; the TZ25 sample is heterogeneous and partly in the Galactic plane; only 10 dimmers are campaign-class field dwarfs. (b) Completeness-corrected companion fraction at 100-20,000 au with 95 percent profile intervals for dimmers and controls.

Rank of each dimmer among its matched controls for RUWE, tangential velocity and Gaia G flux-over-error (low rank = variable in Gaia DR3). Dashed line: uniform distribution expected if dimmers equal controls. RUWE and velocity ranks are uniform; many dimmers were variable in Gaia DR3.

Odds ratios of eight binarity indicators for all 91 dimmers against matched controls, with 95 percent profile intervals. Companion rows also show search limits of 5,000 and 50,000 au. Counts (observed / expected) are for the main 20,000 au search. Open symbols: no dimmer has the indicator.
